actions.justification: MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle. Patient has septic shock; lactate measurement guides resuscitation intensity and risk stratification. Must be done within 60 minutes.
MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle. Blood cultures must be obtained BEFORE antibiotics to identify causative organism. Critical to do this immediately before antibiotic administration.

MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle. Broad-spectrum antibiotics must be given within 1 hour of septic shock recognition. Patient has penicillin anaphylaxis — select non-penicillin agents (e.g., meropenem + vancomycin or azithromycin-based regimen). Administer immediately after blood cultures.
MANDATORY Hour-1 Bundle action: patient has hypotension (MAP 54, BP 78/42) which is an absolute indication for rapid 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid resuscitation per SSC guidelines.

Patient has refractory hypotension (MAP 54, well below target of 65 mmHg). Norepinephrine is the first-line vasopressor per SSC guidelines for septic shock. Should be initiated to maintain MAP ≥ 65 mmHg.

Patient shows signs of multi-organ dysfunction (confusion, hypotension, hypoxia SpO2 89%, tachycardia). Organ dysfunction assessment is critical to guide resuscitation intensity and identify end-organ damage.
MAP remains critically low at 54 mmHg (target ≥65) despite fluids and norepinephrine. Serial vital sign assessment is essential to track response to resuscitation and guide vasopressor titration.

Patient remains hypotensive (MAP 54) despite norepinephrine initiation and fluid resuscitation. SSC guidelines support adding vasopressin as a second vasopressor to achieve MAP ≥65 mmHg in refractory septic shock.

Identifying the infection source is critical to ensure appropriate antibiotic coverage (especially important given penicillin anaphylaxis limiting antibiotic options) and to guide source control interventions per SSC guidelines.

Patient remains in septic shock with MAP 54, HR 128, SpO2 89%, and lactate 6.1. After fluids and vasopressors (norepinephrine + vasopressin), reassess perfusion to evaluate hemodynamic response and guide further resuscitation.

Initial lactate is critically elevated at 6.1 mmol/L. SSC guidelines mandate serial lactate measurements to guide resuscitation and assess response to treatment. Trend is essential for prognostication.

Patient has refractory hypotension on dual vasopressors. Arterial line provides continuous beat-to-beat BP monitoring essential for titrating vasopressor therapy and frequent blood sampling in septic shock.
CBC is essential to evaluate for leukocytosis/leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia in the context of confirmed gram-negative E. coli bacteremia and septic shock, guiding further management.
BMP needed to assess renal function (AKI common in septic shock), electrolytes, glucose, and BUN/creatinine given severe hypotension and organ dysfunction risk.
Coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT) are critical to screen for DIC, which is a serious complication of gram-negative septic shock with lactate 6.1 mmol/L.
Procalcitonin is a useful biomarker for monitoring response to antibiotic therapy in gram-negative septic shock; serial measurements can guide antibiotic de-escalation decisions.

Patient remains hemodynamically unstable (MAP 54, HR 128) despite initial 30mL/kg bolus and vasopressors. Additional crystalloid fluid boluses are indicated to support ongoing resuscitation guided by dynamic response.
Chest X-ray is indicated to evaluate for pulmonary source of infection, assess for fluid overload from aggressive resuscitation, and evaluate SpO2 of 89% with RR 28.

Patient is on dual vasopressors (norepinephrine and vasopressin) with persistent septic shock (MAP 54, lactate 6.1). A central line is indicated for reliable vasopressor administration, CVP monitoring, and ongoing resuscitation management. This is the only remaining available action and is clinically appropriate given the severity of illness.

MANDATORY action: Patient remains in septic shock with MAP 54 (target ≥65 mmHg), HR 128, BP 78/42. Although norepinephrine and vasopressin have been started, this mandatory action must be completed to confirm vasopressor therapy is active and titrated appropriately for refractory hypotension.

Patient has septic shock with lactate 6.1, confirmed gram-negative E. coli bacteremia, MAP <65 despite vasopressors, SpO2 89%, and confusion — all indicating critical illness requiring ICU-level monitoring and care.

violation_events.description: Action start_vasopressor_if_hypotensive performed 35 min after deadline
